beginner.summary: For system administrators, Java developers and DevOps engineers who are new to Apache Tomcat. Covers installing Tomcat 10.1 and 11 on Linux and Windows, CATALINA_HOME and CATALINA_BASE, server.xml, connectors, WAR deployment and context descriptors, the Manager application, users and roles, JULI and access logging, JVM options with setenv.sh, sessions, error pages, Maven-driven deployment and a capstone that stands up a complete instance for a Jakarta EE sample application.
prerequisites: Comfortable in a Linux shell or PowerShell: editing files, setting environment variables, reading logs with tail and grep
Basic Java knowledge: can explain what a JAR, a WAR and a JDK are and can run java -version
A Linux VM, WSL2 or Windows machine with administrator or sudo rights, outbound internet access and a JDK 17 or 21 available to install
outcomes: Install, start, stop and run Tomcat 10.1 and 11 as a managed service with separate CATALINA_HOME and CATALINA_BASE directories
Read and edit server.xml, context descriptors and web.xml to configure connectors, hosts and applications
Deploy, undeploy and redeploy Jakarta EE WAR files by hand, with the Manager application and from Maven
Configure users, roles, logging, JVM memory options and error pages, and diagnose the most common startup failures from the logs

outcomes: Plan and execute a javax to jakarta migration of applications and their libraries onto Tomcat 10.1 or 11 with measured evidence
Design clustered and load-balanced Tomcat tiers with a deliberate session strategy and rolling, zero-downtime upgrades
Harden Tomcat against common attack classes, limit request abuse and respond to published CVEs within a defined process
Diagnose stuck threads, leaks and latency problems with thread dumps, heap dumps and Flight Recorder, and extend Tomcat with custom valves and realms
